Title: [Excerpt from] Vote for Our Zoo
Author: by Lori Mortensen
Content: Jamie ran through the zoo gate with her friend Sam. “I love the zoo!” she cried....
But then Jamie saw a poster. “Oh, no, Sam,” she said. “This field trip to the zoo might be our last!”
“What do you mean?” asked Sam.

Jamie read, “Save our zoo! Vote 'yes' on `text(November 4)`!” She shook her head. “The city is having a special vote to raise money for the zoo. If people vote 'no, there won't be a city zoo anymore.”
“We can't let that happen,” Sam said. “How much money does the zoo need? Maybe we could have a bake sale.”
Jamie sighed. “The poster says the zoo needs `text(four million dollars)`.”
“Wow!” said Sam. “We'd have to sell a lot of cookies to make that much money.”
“The poster says the zoo's cages are too small. And they're falling apart,” Jamie said. “The zoo needs money to rebuild. Without money, the zoo will have to close.”
Jamie looked around. If she were an animal, she'd want to live in a newer place `text(ten)` times bigger. “I'd vote for a new zoo,” she said, “if I could vote.”
“Me, too” said Sam. “I wish we were older.”
Then Jamie had an idea. “Maybe we don't need to vote” she said.
“What do you mean?” asked Sam,
“Instead of voting, we'll campaign,” Jamie said. “We'll get everyone in town who can vote to vote for the zoo.”
:box:campaign = ask people to vote for something
“Great idea,” said Sam. “But how will we do that?”
“Remember when the new principal came?” asked Jamie.
“Sure” said Sam. “We tied tons of ribbons on the school's fence.”
“This time we'll spell out 'Save Our Zoo!' with ribbons,” said Jamie.
“We could make posters, too,” said Sam. “I'm great at making posters.”...
The `text(next day)`, Jamie's class tied green ribbons to the playground fence. The ribbons spelled out “Save Our Zoo!...
By the end of the `text(week)`, Jamie and her class had `text(dozens)` of posters and fliers. They put them in stores and in their front yards.
“Do you think it will work?” asked Sam.
“I hope so,” said Jamie. “We have to save the zoo.”
That night, Jamie and her family went to a special town meeting. The city council held the meeting so people could talk about the vote. Jamie hoped everyone wanted to save the zoo like she did.
:box:city council = group of people who are chosen to make decisions for the city
But some people had other ideas.
“We have a set amount of money,” said Mr. Li. “I think the city should use the money to make the library bigger.”
“We should build a new fire station” said Mrs. Bradley.
“We need a new soccer field,” said Mrs. Lopez.
Jamie realized there were many ways to spend `text(four million dollars)`. People needed fire stations, libraries, and soccer fields, too.

On voting day, Jamie worried. She watched people going in and out of the school library to vote. Her school was `text(one)` of many polling sites in the city. Every neighborhood had its own polling site....
:box:polling sites = places where people vote
The next morning, Jamie raced outside to get the newspaper....
Jamie's heart sank. The zoo had lost. She wished her class could have campaigned longer. What would happen to the animals now?

“I'm sorry, Jamie,” said her mother. “But look! After the zoo closes, all of the animals will go to the Heritage Wildlife Preserve. The animals will have lots of space there. And it's only a few `text(hours)` away.”
:box:wildlife preserve = area of land where animals are protected
“The zoo lost the vote,” said Jamie, “but I guess the animals won.”
